scope: The Kitty animation carrier of the owned suite, collected alone in one persistent (KeepOnClose) tab on a disposable macOS sidecar: the pane is a client of the multiplexer daemon and the worker is the daemon's child. The same four bounded cases as the direct-tab publication (stationary control, playback, stop-freeze, PNG and root-based frames) over paired original offscreen PNGs, complete cells/modes and wall-clock capture spans. No stock collector ran in this run, so there is no stock grade and no Core or common-harness claim; the pinned callbacks are replayed from the retained bundle and stay inconclusive by design. Not measured: a reattach or restart (restore from a snapshot), a second client, remote persistent sessions, other platforms, a non-PNG root, frame-rate or display-refresh cadence.

effectContract.statement: In a persistent tab, whose shell runs in the multiplexer daemon and whose pane is a client of it, the same animation behaviour as in a direct tab: A retained 16x16 raw RGBA image with two further frames added by a=f (z=5000 ms each, root gap 5000 ms) shows its root frame, stays on it past that gap while stopped, then after a=a,s=3 shows the second frame, the third frame and the root frame again at the times its gaps give (measured by paired offscreen captures against the App's wall clock), and after a=a,s=1 stays frozen on the frame it was showing past a hold that would have advanced it. A half-transparent PNG frame (a=f,f=100) built over the root frame (c=1) shows the protocol's straight-alpha blend of the two when chosen with a=a,c=; after the root is edited (a=f,r=1) and shown again, a second PNG frame built over it shows the blend of the edited pixels instead of the original. Every write is acknowledged OK and every cleared target is blank again.
